stories.title: Norse Atlantic Airways halts flights and files for bankruptcy

articles.headline: Norse Atlantic airline suspends all flights, on brink of bankruptcy amid rising fuel costs
articles.snippet: Norse Atlantic suspended all flights as its board warned it may file for bankruptcy without urgent short-term financing, leaving PIA passengers stranded.

articles.headline: Another blow for European airline after all flights are cancelled
articles.snippet: Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights amid a critical financial situation, with the airline warning it could file for bankruptcy unless an urgent solution to its finances is found.

articles.snippet: Norse Atlantic Airways finds itself in dire straits, grappling with severe financial challenges stemming from lease terminations for its Boeing 787 fleet. After halting all operations on November 26…

articles.headline: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
articles.snippet: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic…

articles.headline: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights
articles.snippet: Norwegian airline tells customers not to come to airports after surging fuel costs caused by Iran war ruin finances Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights…

agreed_facts.text: Norse Atlantic Airways suspended or cancelled all its flights.
The airline faces bankruptcy because of its financial situation.
Rising aviation fuel costs are cited as a cause of the airline's financial problems.
The fuel cost rise is attributed to the war in Iran.

headline_quotes.quote: Another blow for European airline after all flights are cancelled
files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights

emphasis.text: Leads with the cancellation of all flights and the airline's critical financial situation.
Reports the airline told customers not to come to airports.
Attributes the airline's ruined finances to surging fuel costs caused by the Iran war.

headline_quotes.quote: succumbing to aviation fuel costs

emphasis.text: Describes Norse Atlantic as a low-cost airline founded only a few years ago that had struggled to turn a profit.
Attributes the collapse to a spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran.

headline_quotes.quote: on brink of bankruptcy amid rising fuel costs
leaving PIA passengers stranded

emphasis.text: Reports the board warned it may file for bankruptcy without urgent short-term financing.
Highlights PIA passengers left stranded by the suspension.

summary.text: Norse Atlantic Airways halted all flights, with one report dating the halt to 26 November. Some outlets report the Norwegian airline has filed for bankruptcy; earlier reports say it warned it might file without urgent financing. Reports cite rising fuel costs or lease terminations for its Boeing 787 fleet.

conclusion.text: All coverage agrees Norse Atlantic halted flights and faces bankruptcy. Western outlets attribute this to fuel costs, some linking them to the Iran war, while the Eastern outlet focuses on lease terminations for its 787 fleet. Reports differ on whether it has filed for bankruptcy or only warned it might.

stories.title: UK contacts 100,000 reservists to prepare for possible war

articles.headline: UK military chiefs write to 100,000 reservists telling them to prepare for war
articles.snippet: The move follows increasing threats from Vladimir Putin, and marks the first time since the Cold War that reservists have been urged to get ready for war

articles.headline: 'The steady drumbeat of war is growing louder - here's how Britain is being put on notice'
articles.snippet: OPINION: 'The government has subtly been warning UK troops and civilians to prepare for an escalation in conflict and finally the message appears to be coming through - with troops put on standby

articles.headline: UK shields fighter jets, contacts reservists in Cold War-scale push amid Russia threat
articles.snippet: Wes Streeting says the United Kingdom is contacting former service members to update its strategic reserve as Russian sabotage rises across Europe.

articles.headline: MoD can't find contact details for half of veterans
articles.snippet: The Ministry of Defence has published open letters to almost 100,000 veterans about their duty to mobilise in a crisis but it appears unable to find many people's direct contact details.

articles.headline: Military can't find HALF of its army of veteran reservists who may be called up if Britain goes to war
articles.snippet: The UK has almost 100,000 people in its so-called 'strategic reserve', who were this week told to prepare for war in the biggest drive of its kind since the Cold War.

agreed_facts.text: Almost 100,000 reservists or veterans have been contacted about preparing for war or mobilising in a crisis.
The UK is contacting former service members as part of its strategic reserve.
The move is described as the first or biggest of its kind since the Cold War.
The move is linked to threats from Russia or Vladimir Putin.
The military cannot find contact details for about half of the veterans.

headline_quotes.quote: telling them to prepare for war
The steady drumbeat of war is growing louder

emphasis.text: Leads with the instruction to prepare for war, linking it to increasing threats from Vladimir Putin.
Presents it as the first time since the Cold War reservists have been urged to get ready for war.

headline_quotes.quote: MoD can't find contact details for half of veterans

emphasis.text: Leads with the Ministry of Defence being unable to find direct contact details for many of the veterans.
Describes the letters as open letters about veterans' duty to mobilise in a crisis.

headline_quotes.quote: Cold War-scale push amid Russia threat
Military can't find HALF of its army of veteran reservists

emphasis.text: Links the move to rising Russian sabotage across Europe and mentions the UK shielding fighter jets.
Attributes the statement on contacting former service members to Wes Streeting.
Leads with the military being unable to find half of its veteran reservists.

omissions.text: Left coverage does not mention that the military cannot find contact details for about half of the veterans.
Centre coverage does not mention Russia or Putin as the context for the move.
Centre coverage does not mention the comparison with the Cold War.

opinion.text: A Daily Mirror opinion piece argues the government has subtly been warning troops and civilians to prepare for an escalation in conflict, with troops put on standby.

headline_quotes.quote: UK military chiefs write to 100,000 reservists telling them to prepare for war
MoD can't find contact details for half of veterans

emphasis.text: Emphasises the scale of the call to prepare for war and its Cold War comparison.
Emphasises the gap in contact details for about half of the veterans.

summary.text: The UK has contacted almost 100,000 former service members in its strategic reserve, telling them to prepare for war in what is described as the biggest such move since the Cold War, amid threats from Russia. Reports say the Ministry of Defence cannot find direct contact details for about half of them.

conclusion.text: All coverage agrees the UK has contacted about 100,000 former service members to prepare for possible war. Left and right outlets frame it around the Russian threat and Cold War comparison, while centre and one right outlet lead with the MoD being unable to find half of them. No claims are disputed between outlets.

stories.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie convicted over 123 more deaths

articles.headline: Kenyan cult leader in jail for 191 murders convicted over another 123 deaths
articles.snippet: A Kenyan cult leader has been convicted of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 of his followers, having already been found guilty of murdering 191 others.

articles.headline: Kenyan cult leader serving 200-year sentence is convicted again over 123 more deaths
articles.snippet: Paul Mackenzie, who led an apocalyptic church cult in Kenya and ordered his followers to stop eating, and has been convicted over the deaths of 123 more people

articles.snippet: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

agreed_facts.text: A Kenyan cult leader has been convicted over the deaths of a further 123 people.
He had already been convicted and jailed for earlier killings before this verdict.
The cult leader is named as Paul Mackenzie.
He is already serving a 200-year sentence.
The deaths are linked to starvation of followers.

headline_quotes.quote: serving 200-year sentence is convicted again over 123 more deaths
ordered his followers to stop eating

weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children

summary.text: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been convicted over the deaths of 123 more of his followers. He was already jailed for earlier murders, with outlets giving 191 or 190 victims and reporting a 200-year sentence.

conclusion.text: All outlets report Paul Mackenzie's new conviction over 123 deaths on top of an earlier murder conviction. The left and right lead with his 200-year sentence and starvation, the centre with manslaughter and child victims. The earlier victim count differs between 191 and 190.
